scams.name: IAH & Hobby Airport Rideshare & Fake-Driver Scam
scams.tldr: Unlicensed drivers impersonate Uber and Lyft pickups at both Bush Intercontinental and Hobby airports, targeting arriving tourists with fabricated fares.
scams.description: Unlicensed drivers impersonate Uber and Lyft pickups at both Bush Intercontinental and Hobby airports, targeting arriving tourists with fabricated fares.
scams.avoidance: Walk past every driver who approaches you inside the terminal, at baggage claim, or on the arrivals curb without pausing. Verify the license plate, vehicle make, and driver name in the Uber or Lyft app before opening any door. Use only the designated rideshare pickup zone at your terminal; IAH posts them at Gate A8, B8, C45, D8, and E1. Never accept a "your driver canceled, I will take you instead" pitch, because legitimate rideshare platforms do not operate that way. If you are pressured or your luggage is held, photograph the plate and call IAH/Hobby Airport Police or the Houston Police at 713-884-3131.
scams.location: George Bush Intercontinental Airport (IAH) Terminals A-E rideshare pickup zones, Hobby Airport baggage-claim curbs, IAH Terminal E international arrivals, Terminal C rental-car corridor

scams.name: Rodeo Houston & NRG Stadium Event Parking Scam
scams.tldr: Unofficial "parking attendants" direct arriving drivers into private lots, vacant yards, or unauthorized strips of street parking, demanding $40 to $80 in cash for spots that are illegal, tow-prone, or worth nothing.
scams.description: Unofficial "parking attendants" direct arriving drivers into private lots, vacant yards, or unauthorized strips of street parking, demanding $40 to $80 in cash for spots that are illegal, tow-prone, or worth nothing.
scams.avoidance: Prepay for NRG or Toyota Center parking on the official venue website before driving to the event. Keep driving past any street "attendant" waving you into a residential yard or unmarked lot near NRG Park. Use only parking lots with electronic gates, posted prices, and uniformed event-day staff wearing venue badges. Pay by credit card when possible so a chargeback is available if the lot turns out to be illegitimate. If your car is towed from an unofficial lot, call the Houston Police non-emergency line at 713-884-3131 for a towed-vehicle lookup.
scams.location: NRG Stadium parking lots, NRG Park gates on Kirby Drive, Houston Livestock Show perimeter, residential streets near South Main/Kirby, Houston Astros Daikin Park event-day approaches, Toyota Center Rockets game-day perimeter

scams.name: Post-Ride Uber & Lyft 'Vomit Scam' Fake Cleaning-Fee Charge
scams.tldr: This scheme is still active, with identical Houston-area reports surfacing three and four years after it first appeared.
scams.description: This scheme is still active. Identical Houston-area reports continue to surface three and four years after the scam first appeared: a driver falsely claims a rider was sick in the vehicle and adds a bogus cleaning fee to the fare after the trip ends.
scams.avoidance: Take a quick phone photo of the interior of every Uber or Lyft just before you exit, timestamping the clean seats and floor. Review the trip receipt in the Uber or Lyft app within 48 hours and dispute any unexpected cleaning fee immediately. Refuse to accept a "rerouting" or "wait" fee added after the trip, because the in-app fare quoted at booking is the contract. If Uber or Lyft decline the dispute, file a credit-card chargeback citing services not rendered and attach the exit photo. Report repeat-offender drivers to the City of Houston Property and Financial Crimes Division at 713-308-3300.
scams.location: IAH and Hobby Airport Uber/Lyft trips, downtown Houston rideshare drop-offs, Midtown and Montrose late-night rides, Galleria district weekend rideshare, Rice Village and The Heights evening trips

scams.name: Fake 'Uber Support' Verification-Code Account Takeover
scams.tldr: Callers posing as Uber support phone from a spoofed Uber number and trick riders into reading out a verification code, taking over their account.
scams.description: Fake "support" calls from a spoofed Uber number trick riders into reading out a verification code sent to their phone, which hands the caller control of the account. Houston Uber drivers and riders alike report being targeted by these calls.
scams.avoidance: Never read a verification code aloud to any caller claiming to be Uber, Lyft, or bank support, because these services never ask for one. Hang up immediately on any inbound call claiming "unusual activity" and open the Uber or Lyft app directly to check your account. If you accidentally share a code, change your Uber or Lyft password within 60 seconds and remove your stored payment methods. Report the takeover at uber.com/safety or lyft.com/safety and dispute any fraudulent charges with your card issuer. File a report with the FTC at reportfraud.ftc.gov and with the Houston Property and Financial Crimes Division at 713-308-3300.
scams.location: Houston-area Uber and Lyft rides, IAH Airport rideshare wait zones, downtown hotel rideshare pickups, Montrose and Midtown late-night rides, University of Houston and Rice University campus rideshare
